newsitem.title: UK: UK NATURAL GAS MARKET HEADS LOWER, FOCUS ON Q1.
newsitem.headline: UK NATURAL GAS MARKET HEADS LOWER, FOCUS ON Q1.

text.p: The British natural gas market eased lower on Friday as traders took profits, with activity concentrated on the first quarter of next year.

Q1 traded more than half a dozen times, hitting a low of 16.95 pence a therm early in the day. The market then bounced slightly and the quarter traded at a high of 17.05 pence, still below Thursday's levels.
"We saw Q1 trickling down slightly as people took profits but then the shorts came in and it recovered a bit," said one trader.
Some traders believed that Q1 has been overvalued for the last week or so.
Prompt gas eased back with a weekend deal done at 9.25 pence. September, October and November headed in the same direction, and Q4 traded at a low of 13.20 pence.
A similar pattern was followed on the IPE screen, where new extended trading hours were introduced on Friday. A balance of month contract was also introduced, but failed to trade on its first day.
